setup.crime: Port Calder, a rainy harbor town. Silas Crane reports $90k stolen from his shipping company's safe. You are a newly promoted detective with 3 days before the next cargo ship sails and the money leaves with it. The Tidewater Syndicate has been washing cash through the fish market for months, and somebody inside the harbor is protecting it.
setup.friendly: Port Calder is getting ready for the Gold Coin Festival, but the prize chest is empty! The sneaky Tidewater Gang is hiding the coins somewhere by the harbor. You have 3 days before their boat sails away. Some people will help you, and some will try to trick you.

blurb.crime: Courier who moves the cash. Smooth talker.
blurb.friendly: Runs errands for the gang. Very smooth talker.

blurb.crime: Dock foreman. Looks guilty, keeps to himself.
Runs the fish market. Busy, sharp, sometimes rushed.
blurb.friendly: Runs the fish market. Always in a hurry.

blurb.crime: Night guard on the docks. Leaving town soon.
blurb.friendly: Night guard on the docks. Going on a trip soon.

blurb.crime: Knows everyone. Sells what he hears, to anyone.
blurb.friendly: Knows everybody's business. Will tell you things... for a favor.

blurb.crime: Owns Crane Shipping. Reported the theft himself.
blurb.friendly: Owns the big shipping company. He reported the missing coins.

blurb.crime: Forensic accountant. Sees patterns in totals.
Your old partner. Patient, explains his thinking.
blurb.friendly: Your old detective buddy. Great at explaining.

blurb.crime: Forensic analyst. One sure answer, no guesswork.
blurb.friendly: Science detective. Can find one answer for sure.

blurb.crime: Undercover cop inside the syndicate. Can confirm one claim.
blurb.friendly: A secret helper inside the gang. Can check if someone told the truth.

intro.crime: Rosa keeps a cash book for the market. Somebody has been writing in it at night. Work out who moved how much each hour.
intro.friendly: Rosa's notebook has numbers in it from last night. Work out how many coins each person carried each hour.

fact.crime: Cash moves through the fish market every night, and Vex carries the biggest bags.
fact.friendly: The coins go through the fish market at night, and Vex carries the most.

intro.crime: The dock cameras caught a few people in a few rooms. Juno was on duty. Work out who was in which room each hour. Rooms are numbered along the pier.
intro.friendly: The cameras saw some people in some rooms. Work out who was in which room each hour. Rooms are numbered along the pier.

fact.crime: Vex was inside Warehouse 9 at midnight, not at home as he claims.
fact.friendly: Vex was in Warehouse 9 at midnight. He said he was at home!

intro.crime: Tip hands over his payment records, a little too eagerly. Work out the payments and check what Tip says about them.
intro.friendly: Tip gives you his notes. He seems very keen to help. Check if what he says matches the numbers.

fact.crime: Every payment ends up in an account owned by Crane Shipping. Tip lied to cover it.
fact.friendly: All the coins go to the shipping company. Tip fibbed to hide it!

intro.crime: Hidden in Warehouse 9: a private ledger in Crane's handwriting. Crack it and the whole trail is exposed.
intro.friendly: Hidden in Warehouse 9: a secret book in Mr. Crane's handwriting! Crack it to solve the case.

fact.crime: Crane staged the theft. The $90k never left his company. It was washed through the market to pay the syndicate.
fact.friendly: Mr. Crane hid the coins himself and blamed someone else!

rumor.crime: Juno's bus ticket is for the start of Day 2.
rumor.friendly: Juno is going on a trip at the start of Day 2.

message.crime: Juno has left town. Tracking her down for her statement will cost time and a favor.
message.friendly: Juno went on her trip! You can still call her, but it costs time and a favor.

rumor.crime: Word on the docks: someone wants Warehouse 9 gone.
rumor.friendly: Somebody wants to mess up Warehouse 9.

message.crime: Warehouse 9 burned overnight. Tip told someone. The ledger survived, but rebuilding the trail costs an extra hour.
message.friendly: Warehouse 9 got flooded! Tip told the gang. Finding the secret book now takes an extra hour.

rumor.crime: The cargo ship sails at the end of Day 3.
rumor.friendly: The gang's boat leaves at the end of Day 3.

message.crime: The ship is leaving. Make your accusation now.
message.friendly: The boat is leaving! Time to say who did it.

text.crime: "Warehouse 9 is where they keep the books. Give me one favor and I'll keep an eye on it for you. Nobody touches it. You have my word."
text.friendly: "Give me one favor and I'll guard Warehouse 9 for you. Promise!"

accept.crime: Tip grins and pockets the favor.

message.crime: Something about Rosa's story bothered you, and your instinct is off this time. Her cash book is accurate, so take her at her word.
message.friendly: Rosa's notebook is right and your hunch was wrong. Trust her and look again!

message.crime: Kane's gruff manner put you on edge. That is not evidence. His statement holds up, so take him at his word.
message.friendly: Kane is grumpy, but he's telling the truth! Try again.

message.crime: Juno clocked out and left town before you reached her. Her camera notes are gone unless you track her down.
message.friendly: Juno went on holiday before you asked her. Find her to get her notes back!

message.crime: Vex talked her way past you, and you let her. Smooth talk is not an alibi. Check which room she says she was in.
message.friendly: Vex says some silly things. Check her room again!

message.crime: You haven't cracked the dock camera log yet. Whoever was in those rooms is the one you need to know about. Don't point the finger yet.
message.friendly: The camera log still has secrets. Solve it first!

message.crime: Tip was too eager to help, and you took his word for it. Keen helpers often sell what they hear. Recheck his payments.
message.friendly: Tip is very eager to help. Check his notes carefully!

message.crime: You never checked all of Tip's payments. A double agent hides in the lines you skipped. Go back and mark every one.
message.friendly: Did you check all of Tip's notes? Look again!

message.crime: Vex lies to protect the boss, and you believed her anyway. Her word can't open this ledger. Mark her statements again.
message.friendly: Vex fibbed to protect her boss. Look at her words again!

message.crime: Rosa made an honest mistake in her ledger, and in this case the mistake hides the truth. You took it at face value. Check the numbers again.
Warehouse 9 burned overnight. The harbormaster's ledger survived, but tracing it now costs you extra hours. You should have opened it sooner.
message.friendly: The warehouse burned, but the book is safe. It will take more time!

message.crime: You never cracked the harbormaster's ledger. Without it you can't tie the warehouse to the boss. Open it first.
message.friendly: The harbormaster's book still has secrets. Open it first!

message.crime: Tip swore he would guard Warehouse 9 for one favor, and it burned anyway. Never trust a man who sells his promises.
message.friendly: Tip promised to guard Warehouse 9, but it still burned!

message.crime: You are about to accuse someone whose statements you never checked. Read what they told you before you point the finger.
message.friendly: Check what they told you before you point!

message.crime: You have the boss in your sights, but the proof is incomplete. Tip's record still hides a double-agent lie. Expose it first, or Crane walks.
message.friendly: Crane is close, but Tip's secret is still hidden. Find it first!

text.crime: Crane is arrested on the dock with the ledger in evidence. Vex and Tip both turn state's witness. The Tidewater Syndicate is finished in Port Calder.
text.friendly: Mr. Crane is caught! The coins go back to the festival, and the Tidewater Gang is done for.

text.crime: You made an arrest, but without the full trail Crane's lawyers tear the case apart. The ship sails on schedule.
text.friendly: You caught a helper, but the boss got away on the boat.

text.crime: You arrested an innocent person. The syndicate couldn't have planned it better.
text.friendly: That person didn't do it! The gang is laughing all the way to their boat.
